measurement: ffmpeg gdigrab, the spec's fallback capture candidate
why: Verification rejected closing this by documentation: C7 is a capture criterion, OBS's verdict is FAIL on it, and gdigrab offers no audio device at all. Measured against the SAME committed criteria.

ffmpeg.version: ffmpeg version 9.0-full_build-www.gyan.dev Copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers

window.title: [Extension Development Host] Dabbler UAT fixture workspace

capture.argv: ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -f gdigrab -framerate 30 -draw_mouse 1 -i title=[Extension Development Host] Dabbler UAT fixture workspace -t 8 -y D:\Projects\dabbler-ai-orchestration\tools\dabbler-ai-orchestration\.walkthrough-runs\ffmpeg-fallback\capture.mp4

frameContent.method: every pixel of the captured PNG decoded and reduced to luminance
frameContent.conclusion: gdigrab produced a UNIFORMLY BLACK frame. This is the documented GDI failure on hardware-accelerated windows, and it is why the operator ruling of 2026-08-15 made OBS the primary candidate.

C1.note: A correlation of exactly 0 is what the instrument returns for a zero-variance frame. The frame is entirely black, so gdigrab captured NOTHING of the target window. This is the most basic capture requirement and it is not met.

C2.note: No occluder pixels leaked -- but no pixels of any kind were captured. A leakage test over a black frame passes for the wrong reason and must not be read as a pass.

C3.note: gdigrab sized the capture to the window correctly. It is the right-sized picture of nothing.

C7.note: gdigrab offers no audio device, so the container carries a video stream and nothing else. This is the one clause OBS structurally could not satisfy, and the fallback satisfies it.

evaluation.summary: The fallback satisfies the clause OBS cannot (C7, no audio track) and fails the clause that matters most (C1, it captures nothing at all). It is not a usable substitute, and the measurement confirms the operator ruling that made OBS primary rather than overturning it.
